sections.title: A new -t- marker, on top of endings you already know
sections.content: To put a regular verb in the past tense, add -t- (or -ott-/-ett-/-ött- when the stem needs a linking vowel) right after the stem, then the same kind of personal ending you already use elsewhere. dolgozik ("to work") becomes dolgoztam, dolgoztál, dolgozott... — notice the -ik disappears completely; in the past tense every verb, -ik or not, conjugates the same way.

items.english: We studied at home all day.

sections.content: Watch the 3rd person singular closely: dolgozott needs the linking vowel -ott- because dolgoz- ends in a consonant that can't take a bare -t. tanult, on the other hand, needs nothing extra — tanul- already ends in a sound (l) that -t attaches to directly. You'll get a feel for which is which the more forms you see; when in doubt, the -ott-/-ett-/-ött- version is usually safer for 3rd person singular.
